Detail: Global = mean of the mandatory dimensions of the event (equal weights unless stated).
Evaluated independently of the global score. Sub-skills inside a dimension (unit listening checks): see P06.
A dimension below 70% fails the event even if the global score is ≥80%.

Rule: Mandatory dimensions: Reading (unseen text), Writing, Speaking.
Detail: Specified per lesson in Lesson_Practice_Assessment. Writing and Speaking are scored with the Rubrics sheet (lesson rubrics RB-LW-*, RB-LS-*, read with Rubric_Calibration for the level); dimension score = mean of its criteria. Guided practice, independent production and the conversation segment are formative and never scored for progression. Speaking (lesson assessments; also level exits, P07): the voice agent ends the Speaking after a number of learner turns per level (A1 6, A2 7, B1 8, B2 9, C1 10), with a safety maximum of 6 min (A1), 7 min (A2), 9 min (B1), 11 min (B2) or 13 min (C1); the minutes stated in each spec are indicative. If the voice agent malfunctions during the Speaking (output unrelated to the situation, leaving the role, or helping/correcting the learner), the attempt is void: it is not scored or counted, and a new Speaking is run. Writing: the word range sets a minimum; longer texts are not penalized for length (owner decision 2026-10-27).

Applies to: Review checkpoint and level final review
Rule: Mandatory dimensions: Reading, Writing, Speaking; items tagged by grammar section.
Detail: Same thresholds as P01–P03; additionally every reviewed section scoring <70% is flagged for targeted reinforcement (gap detection). Checkpoints follow the diagnostic-first session flow in Review_Plan › Session flow (owner decision 2026-10-21, option B). The final review is recall practice and is not the level pass decision.

Rule: Mandatory dimension: Listening; scored sub-skills gist, detail (+ inference/attitude B1–C1).
Detail: Global ≥80% of items. The ≥70% threshold applies only to sub-skills scored with ≥4 items; sub-skills with fewer items count toward the global score only (owner decision 2026-10-21, OI-029). Embedded checks (single-lesson units) use the same rule with 5–6 items. Listening sources: each unit check normally has its own recording. A recording may serve more than one check (as Form A or as the Alternative source) only when no other suitable recording with a direct audio file exists (VOA or ELLLO, full audio, published transcript); each check then has its own items, never copied from the other check, and Listening_Sources › Notes names the other check (owner decision 2026-10-23).

Rule: Mandatory dimensions: Reading, Listening, Writing, Speaking.
Detail: Each ≥70%, global ≥80%, no compensation. C1 Writing and Speaking rubrics include fluency, cohesion, register, flexibility and appropriateness. Passing the exit assessment is the curricular condition for starting the next level.

Rule: Targeted reinforcement, then an equivalent but different task.
Detail: Reinforcement addresses only the failed dimension(s)/sections (e.g., re-teach with new examples, extra guided practice from the lessons where the content was introduced). The retest uses a task of the same construct, level, length and format. A text, recording or prompt may be used up to 3 times per learner (original + 2 repetitions; owner decision 2026-10-21); the items/questions are always new, generated on demand by the tutor agent, and items of earlier attempts are never reused.
Passed dimensions keep their score; the global score is recomputed with the new dimension score.

Rule: Third failure of the same event (original + 2 retests): repeat content, then the attempt counter resets (owner decision).
Detail: Lesson: the whole lesson is repeated in a new session. Level exit assessment: the lessons whose sections or vocabulary the exit showed as not understood (dimension/section scores <70%) are repeated. Unit listening check: one listening reinforcement session with the same recordings and new questions, then a new attempt. After the repetition the learner again has 3 attempts (original + 2 retests). Owner decision 2026-10-21.

Rule: Record per attempt: event ID, form ID, date, score per dimension, global score, decision.
Detail: Specification only. Additionally record per attempt the IDs of texts/recordings/prompts used (with the learner's use count, max 3 – P08) and the items applied, so that items are never repeated. The technical mechanism that locks/unlocks lessons is out of scope.

Rule: The course prepares for general C1 competence; it does not award or promise an official certification.
Detail: Exit assessments are internal curricular assessments, not standardised CEFR exams.

Rule: Outcome-based progression: time is a guide, not a requirement.
Detail: Planned minutes and hours (Lessons, Workload, Course Map) are indicative only. A lesson, unit or level is complete when its success criteria are met (P01–P07), whether this takes less or more time than planned; time spent is recorded but never used as a pass condition (owner decision 2026-10-21).

Rule: Retest forms are generated on demand by the tutor agent.
Detail: First retest (Form B): the recording in Listening_Sources › Alternative source, played in full. Second retest: the Form A or Form B recording again, or another recording chosen at that moment with the same rules (VOA or ELLLO, full audio, published transcript). A recording may be used up to 3 times per learner (P08). For each attempt the tutor writes new items: same number of items, sub-skill mix, item types and MC options as Form A (Listening_Items), every key verifiable in the published transcript; items of earlier attempts are never reused. Owner decisions 2026-10-21 (OI-011; reuse rule).

Rule: Exit forms are generated on demand by the tutor agent from Level_Exit_Assessments.
Detail: For every attempt (Form A, then B and C for retests) the tutor generates the texts, recordings, items and prompts that match the component specification (input, length, task types, items, scoring criteria, pass rule). Reading texts are original and level-controlled; listening uses full external audio with a published transcript (VOA or ELLLO, as for unit checks). A text, recording or prompt may be used up to 3 times per learner (P08); items are always new. Writing and speaking are scored with the exit rubrics (Rubrics RB-XW-*, RB-XS-*). The form ID and its content are recorded per attempt (P11). Owner decision 2026-10-21 (OI-012; reuse rule).

Rule: Adaptive two-stage placement test, max 60 min, run by the tutor agent and scored by the evaluator; the placement decision is computed by code.
Detail: Stage 1 (level, ≈25 min) and Stage 2 (unit, ≈35 min) as specified in Placement_Test. Grammar and vocabulary are both tested. A unit is mastered when grammar ≥70%, vocabulary ≥70% and global ≥80% (same thresholds as P01–P03). Start lesson = first lesson of the first content unit not mastered. Owner decision 2026-10-21.

Rule: Lessons before the start lesson are recorded as "credited by placement"; exit assessments of levels below the placement level are recorded as passed.
Detail: Vocabulary of credited lessons counts as taught (Reading_Specs recycling), except entries failed in the placement sample, which are flagged for priority recycling. Unit listening checks of credited units are not required. Owner decision 2026-10-21.

Rule: One formative session before the start lesson (new session, not scored).
Detail: Covers (a) sections and vocabulary failed in the placement test within credited units and (b) the REQUIRED prerequisites of the start lesson (Prerequisite_Map). Owner decision 2026-10-21.

Rule: The tutor agent may propose re-placement; the learner accepts or rejects.
Detail: Trigger: evidence from the first lessons after placement that the start point is too low or too high (e.g., all dimensions ≥95% in the first lessons, or repeated failures). The tutor gives the evidence and the proposed lesson; if the learner accepts, code records the new start lesson and credits/re-opens lessons accordingly (P17). Owner decision 2026-10-21.
